title: Derived internal-function bar model for condensed group invariants
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $G$ be a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff topological group which is an inverse limit of finite discrete groups. Its condensed group is $\underline G(P)=C(P,G)$ on profinite sets. Use internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; a $G$-equivariant module is an internal module with an $A$-linear $\underline G$-action satisfying the identity and multiplication laws. Let $\Gamma_G$ be its invariant-submodule functor and $R\Gamma_G$ its ordinary total right derived functor to condensed $A$-modules. For an equivariant module $N$ in degree zero, let $A[\underline G^n]$ be the free internal module on $\underline G^n$ and put
$$B_A^n(N)=R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^n],N).$$
Here the internal Hom is derived in its second argument; the cosimplicial maps are those of the inhomogeneous group nerve, with the first face using the given action. There is a natural isomorphism
$$R\Gamma_G(N[0])\cong\operatorname{Tot}_{n\geq0}B_A^n(N).$$
The totalization uses compatible nonnegative resolutions. The degree-zero augmentation is the inclusion of invariants. This isomorphism commutes with maps of equivariant modules and with scalar restriction along a condensed ring map $A\to A'$: the map for $N\to\operatorname{Res}N'$ is induced by that map in every derived internal Hom term. The assertion does not replace derived internal Hom by the underived continuous-function module, and does not identify topological-module cohomology with internal condensed derived invariants. Free internal module means the left adjoint to forgetting a module to a condensed set. Internal module Hom is the right adjoint of internal module tensor; its right derived functor is computed by injective resolutions in its second variable. These are taken in coefficient universes containing the small site and the profinite parameter sets.
